summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI) that offer secure, managed access to multiple foundation models without data leaving the customer's cloud boundary. There is no single winner — the best fit typically follows an organization's existing cloud footprint, with data platforms like Snowflake and Databricks and specialized vendors like IBM watsonx and Oracle competing on governance, data gravity, and industry verticals. All are mature, enterprise-grade options, so selection hinges on model choice, compliance posture, and existing contracts rather than raw capability.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and completions stay within the company's own cloud tenancy/VPC rather than being sent to a third-party vendor API, satisfying regulatory and IP-protection requirements.
Unified compliance and governance: a single platform delivers audit logs, IAM-based access control, encryption, and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO, FedRAMP) across many models at once.
Model choice behind one API: a single integration provides access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT and others, avoiding lock-in to one model provider and enabling easy switching.
Single billing and existing cloud contracts: usage rolls into the enterprise's existing cloud commitment/EDP, consolidating procurement, invoicing, and spend management.
Enterprise operational features: private networking, VPC endpoints, fine-tuning/customization, provisioned throughput, and integration with existing data, security, and MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput (reserved model units) for guaranteed capacity; batch and fine-tuning priced separately.
key_features: 30+ foundation models behind one API
AWS IAM-native identity and access control
VPC/PrivateLink private connectivity
CloudTrail audit logging
Custom model fine-tuning and RAG (Knowledge Bases)
Bedrock Agents and Guardrails
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS wanting the widest model choice and deep AWS-native security integration.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved, predictable capacity.
key_features: Deepest access to OpenAI frontier models
Azure AD / Entra ID identity integration
Private endpoints and VNet isolation
Content filtering and responsible AI controls
Fine-tuning support
Integration with Microsoft 365 and Copilot ecosystem
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first organizations wanting best-in-class OpenAI models within their existing Azure security and productivity stack.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
available_models: Third-party and open-source models via Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Per-token on-demand pricing plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units); e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields roughly 67,250 tokens/second sustained.
key_features: First-party Gemini plus third-party and open models
GSU-based reserved throughput
VPC Service Controls and private connectivity
Cloud Audit Logs
Fine-tuning, distillation, and grounding
Integration with BigQuery and Vertex AI MLOps
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud-centric and data/analytics-heavy enterprises wanting Gemini plus strong data-platform integration.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; LLM functions billed per token processed, bundled into Snowflake compute billing.
key_features: Models run next to governed data inside Snowflake
No data movement out of the Snowflake perimeter
SQL and Python LLM functions (Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search)
Snowflake Horizon governance and RBAC
Document AI and RAG over enterprise data
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data already lives in Snowflake and want AI applied directly to governed data without ETL.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based DBU pricing for model serving, fine-tuning, and foundation model APIs within the Databricks Lakehouse.
key_features: Unity Catalog governance and lineage
Model serving and AI Gateway unifying external and open models
Strong custom fine-tuning and training (Mosaic)
Runs within customer cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP)
RAG and vector search over lakehouse data
platforms.best_for: Data-engineering and ML-heavy enterprises wanting to build and fine-tune models on their own governed lakehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription and consumption-based (Resource Units/tokens); available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data.
key_features: On-prem and hybrid deployment options
watsonx.governance for model risk and compliance
watsonx Orchestrate for multi-platform agent management
IBM Granite indemnified first-party models
Strong focus on regulated industries
platforms.best_for: Highly regulated enterprises and governments needing on-prem/hybrid deployment, AI governance, and indemnified models.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/per-token on-demand pricing plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated capacity
Deep integration with Oracle Fusion/ERP and Oracle Database
OCI IAM and private networking
Sovereign and distributed cloud regions
Fine-tuning support
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises running Fusion/ERP and Oracle databases wanting GenAI close to their ERP data.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Serverless pay-per-use (Neurons/tokens) with a generous free tier; billed within Cloudflare's edge platform.
key_features: Globally distributed edge inference (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, and observability across providers
Serverless, no infrastructure to manage
Data localization and regional inference controls
Tight integration with Workers, R2, and Vectorize
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises wanting low-latency, serverless edge inference over open models with multi-provider gateway control.
